Differential testing compares implementations as pseudo-oracles; agreement cannot establish correctness when both share faulty preprocessing, indexing, or assumptions. Reference independence therefore needs separate computational paths and independently derived expected cases. ML comparisons also require aligned semantics and justified numerical tolerances: a four-framework study found many legitimate implementation differences that obscured bug signals. [Herbold and Tunkel](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10664-022-10273-9). Practical implication: artifact hashes establish identity and provenance; behavioral fault detection requires observable output assertions and demonstrated sensitivity to faults.

Mutation testing measures sensitivity to injected faults, with results dependent on operator realism and mutant selection. ML mutation research explicitly questions whether conventional mutation-testing assumptions transfer to learned models. Equivalent mutants preserve behavior and cannot be killed; surviving sampled inputs alone do not establish equivalence. [Panichella and Liem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01341), [equivalence study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.09241). Recommended evaluation design: separate calibration fixtures from final evaluation, hold out mutation-operator families, report detection by operator, distinguish invalid executions from behavioral kills, and document equivalence judgments. These are methodological recommendations, not guarantees established by the cited studies.

Metamorphic testing supplies complementary checks through justified relationships between executions, reducing dependence on a reference implementation. Its strength depends on the relations and fault population: one classifier study detected only 14.8% of 709 reachable mutants using previously proposed relations. [Saha and Kanewala](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07348). For inference, consider candidate-permutation equivariance and batch partition invariance where the specification guarantees them; preserve sequential order. Combine these with independently calculated small examples and held-out behavioral faults to assess detection beyond reused calibration cases.
